title: Sleep Calculator
summary: Prepping for an early wakeup? Never seem to feel rested? Discover your recommended sleep/wake time with the sleep calculator.
body_text: Sleep Calculator Cycles (Quick Answer) To wake up refreshed, go to bed in 90-minute cycles: 5 cycles = 7.5 hours (ideal) 6 cycles = 9 hours (optimal) Example: Wake at 6:00 AM → Sleep at: 9:00 PM (9 hours) 10:30 PM (7.5 hours) 💡 Tip: Falling asleep takes ~15 minutes, so adjust accordingly. Why are Sleep or Bedtime Calculators Helpful? Struggling to wake up feeling rested? You’re not alone. Many people search for a sleep calculator or bedtime calculation tool to find their “perfect” bedtime based on sleep cycles. But most calculators stop there. They don’t consider what really affects sleep: your habits, stress, unique internal rhythms, and the disconnect between your brain and body that often causes sleep issues. The consequences of poor sleep can affect many aspects of daily life , leading to impaired mental performance and feeling tired and moody. Many people often ask: Is 10pm to 4am enough sleep? Is 11pm to 5am enough sleep? What time should I go to bed if I wake up at 5am? When should I wake up to optimize my sleep cycle? Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert, Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences: “Understanding your personal circadian rhythm is more effective than rigidly sticking to one set schedule.” We go beyond simple timing. Your sleep time calculator result is a starting point, not a standalone solution. We help you understand why knowing your ideal bedtime isn't enough to actually fall asleep faster, stay asleep longer, and wake up refreshed. We connect this timing with science-backed strategies to help you truly optimize your sleep quality, not just your sleep quantity. Wake Up Refreshed—Start With the Right Sleep Calculator with REM Use our free sleep cycle calculator below to find your ideal bedtime or wake-up time, based on natural 90-minute sleep cycles. Then, discover why timing is only one piece of the puzzle, and how proven CBT-I sleep strategies can help you bridge the gap between knowing your ideal bedtime and actually achieving restful sleep. Dr. Areti Vassilopoulos, PsyD — Clinical Psychologist & Sleep Specialist You can't just 'catch up' on sleep. Using a sleep calculator can help you be intentional about your sleep schedule and build a healthier, more consistent routine. How the Sleep Cycle Calculator Works - Best Time To Sleep and Wake Up Here’s the math behind better mornings: Each sleep cycle = ~90 minutes 5 full sleep cycles = ~7.5 hours Count backwards 7.5 hours from your wake-up time to find your optimal bedtime Example: Wake-up time: 6:00 a.m. → Bedtime: 10:30 p.m. Try this bedtime for a week. The goal is to wake naturally 5–10 minutes before your alarm. Still waking with the alarm? Move bedtime earlier by 15 minutes. Waking too early? Shift it later. Try Our Popular Sleep Calculator Sleep Calculator Sleep Calculator Age Range 0-3 Months 4-11 Months 1-2 Years 3-5 Years 6-13 Years 14-17 Years 18-25 Years 26-35 Years 36-45 Years 46-55 Years 56-64 Years 65+ Years Sleep Schedule I want to wake up at... I want to go to bed at... : : Results It typically takes 15 minutes to fall asleep. If you're 26-35 years old and want to wake up refreshed at 8:00 AM , you should go to bed at one of the following times: ‍ Dr. Rachel Reiss, MD, Sleep Expert for Women: Knowing your ideal bedtime based on your wake-up time is one of the simplest yet most powerful ways to align your body with its natural circadian rhythm. A good night's sleep really does start with good timing. What Your Result Means (And What It Doesn’t) Dr. Daniel Jin Blum, Sleep Expert, Clinical Psychologist, Research Assistant Professor of Psychology “Tools like sleep calculators can help people understand their ideal bedtime based on wake time—but they’re just a starting point.” Our ideal bedtime calculator uses your input to align your bedtime with complete sleep cycles, each approximately 90 minutes long. This approach aims to help you wake up during a lighter stage of sleep, rather than disrupting deep sleep or REM sleep , which can reduce grogginess and improve how you feel upon waking. But here’s the crucial point: Even the perfect bedtime can’t fix underlying sleep disorders or poor sleep quality. If you’re lying awake at 2 a.m., waking repeatedly throughout the night, or dragging through the day despite getting “enough” sleep hours, bedtime math alone won’t help. This can cause health problems that can be more severe . Knowing when to go to bed is one thing; being able to fall asleep and stay asleep is another. Sleep Efficiency & Sleep Cycles Explained: Are You Really Sleeping Well? Use this simple formula to estimate your sleep quality: Sleep Efficiency Diagram How Actual Sleep Time is Calculated Total time in bed − Time to fall asleep − Minutes awake during night = Actual sleep time In bed: 7 hours (420 min) Time to fall asleep: 25 min Awake during night: 25 min Actual sleep: 370 min Sleep Efficiency Formula Sleep Efficiency = Actual sleep time ÷ Total time in bed × 100% Sleep efficiency = 370 ÷ 420 = 88% ✅ 💡 Healthy target: 85% or higher ‍ Why Sleep Quality Matters (Not Just Sleep Hours) Eight hours of fragmented, poor-quality sleep isn’t better than six hours of solid, uninterrupted rest. Improving your sleep hygiene—from limiting screens before bed to managing stress effectively—is key to achieving restorative sleep. Regular exercise may improve your sleep quality. You need to learn how to actively improve your sleep quality, addressing the root causes of your sleep issues, rather than just tracking your hours. We empower you with strategies to build a reliable bedtime routine and truly rest. You can also discover 5 effective ways to improve your sleep and explore sleep compression as a technique for improving sleep quality . How Much Sleep Do You Really Need? Recommended Sleep by Age Age Group Recommended Sleep 4–12 months 12–16 hrs 1–2 years 11–14 hrs 3–5 years 10–13 hrs 6–12 years 9–12 hrs 13–18 years 8–10 hrs 18+ years 7+ hrs ‍ But hours alone don’t tell the whole story. Quality and timing matter, too. An average adult goes through several sleep cycles each night, with each cycle lasting about 90 to 120 minutes. To feel your best, aim for at least four complete sleep cycles. For a more precise recommendation, consider using a sleep calculator that factors in your age and bedtime. ‍ How Sleep Works: Cycles, Stages, and Timing Sleep is crucial for nearly every bodily system. Getting enough sleep allows your mind and body to benefit from its restorative effects and helps you avoid the negative consequences of sleep deprivation. Sleep isn’t just one long rest—it’s a series of intricate sleep cycles, each with distinct stages of sleep. Typically, you cycle through all four stages multiple times each night. The first three stages are known as non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep: Stages 1 and 2 are lighter sleep phases where your body and mind begin to relax and slow down. Stage 3 is deep sleep, considered essential for both physical and mental recovery. The fourth stage is rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. During this stage, most of your body is temporarily paralyzed, but brain activity significantly increases, and your eyes move rapidly behind your closed eyelids. This is when the most intense dreaming occurs, which is vital for memory and complex thinking when you're awake. Early in the night, you spend more time in NREM sleep, while later cycles feature more REM sleep. Researchers believe this combination of NREM and REM sleep throughout the night is what allows you to wake up feeling physically and mentally refreshed. When you don't get enough sleep, you disrupt these cycles, preventing you from getting the necessary balance of NREM and REM sleep, which can have significant repercussions for your overall health and well-being. Deep sleep is crucial for physical restoration and growth, while REM sleep supports memory consolidation and memory and mood regulation . Waking mid-cycle, especially during deep sleep, can leave you feeling groggy and disoriented, even if you’ve spent how many hours of sleep in bed. That’s why aligning your bedtime with your natural cycles, as a sleep cycle calculator suggests, matters—but it's just one piece of the puzzle. ‍ Finding Your Ideal Sleep Schedule Your best bedtime truly depends on your individual biology and lifestyle. Some people are natural night owls, while others are early birds. Factors like shift work, parenthood, or even jet lag can significantly impact your circadian rhythm. Many also find themselves needing to "catch up" on sleep on weekends . While a sleep time calculator is a great starting point, flexible, evidence-based support is what makes the real difference in establishing a sustainable, healthy bedtime routine that works for you . Dr. Shiyan Yeo, MD Sleep calculators are useful starting points. When you match your sleep timing with your biology, you improve not just sleep — but mood, energy, and even immune health. Use this sleep calculator table to find the best bedtime based on your wake-up time. Is Your Sleep Good Enough? Ask yourself: Do you wake up tired or groggy? Do you struggle to fall asleep or stay asleep? Do you need naps or caffeine to get through the day? If yes, it’s time to go beyond bedtime math. Why Most Sleep Advice Doesn’t Work You’ve probably tried a lot—cutting back on screens, drinking sleepytime tea, sticking to a strict bedtime. These tips might help a little, but they don’t solve the real problem. Most sleep advice focuses only on surface-level habits. But if your brain and body are stuck in a cycle of poor sleep, stress, and frustration, no amount of lavender oil or early alarms will fix it. The truth is, sleep issues are often driven by how you think about sleep, your emotional responses to restlessness, and patterns that have become wired into your daily routine. That’s why lasting improvement requires more than a checklist—it takes a deeper approach. Tailored Strategies for Better Sleep Sleep Reset combines the insights from your ideal bedtime calculator result with proven behavioral interventions drawn from CBT-I. We teach you to: Strengthen your bedtime routine and create a positive sleep environment. Address the root causes of your sleep issues, including sleep-related anxiety. Rebuild your body’s natural trust in its sleep rhythm. Learn how to get better sleep without pills through sustainable habit changes and explore naturally remedies for sleep . Looking for more than a quick calculation? Join the tends of thousands who’ve discovered that the secret to better sleep isn’t just when you go to bed—it’s how you live before, during, and after. Why CBT-I Is the Gold Standard for Better Sleep Most people struggling with sleep deprivation and deficiency or chronic sleep issues don’t need medication—they need the right habits and mindset. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) is the clinical gold standard for treating sleep problems, with decades of scientific proof. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH) , it’s a drug-free, evidence-based approach that addresses the root causes of sleep difficulties. Sleep Reset’s program uses CBT-I principles to help you: Break the cycle of anxiety and depression around sleep, a common benefit of techniques like sleep compression . Rebuild a reliable bedtime routine. Address issues like circadian rhythm misalignment and persistent sleep difficulties. Improve both sleep quality vs sleep quantity. CBT-I isn’t about willpower—it’s about science. Research by Dr. James B. Maas at the American Psychological Association (APA) and the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) confirms its efficacy. And Sleep Reset brings it to your phone, without pills or side effects, making it easier than ever to learn how to get better sleep without pills . If you're fighting insomnia with CBT for insomnia , you'll find our approach invaluable Standard Sleep Calculators vs. Sleep Reset Feature Standard Sleep Calculator Sleep Reset Calculates ideal bedtime ✓ ✓ Based on sleep cycles ✓ ✓ Personalizes advice ✗ ✓ Tailored to your unique sleep challenges Considers habits, stress, rhythm ✗ ✓ Integrates these into your personalized plan Offers proven CBT-I strategies ✗ ✓ Foundation of our program Helps fix actual sleep issues ✗ ✓ Addresses root causes of poor sleep Real Results From Real Sleep Reset Members "I used to dread bedtime because I knew I wouldn't fall asleep. With Sleep Reset, I fall asleep faster and wake up feeling human again." —Maya, 37 "The sleep calculator was a helpful start, but the real change came from fixing my bedtime routine and stress habits. I'm finally sleeping through the night." —Josh, 44 "I used to think how many hours of sleep was enough. Now I know it’s not just about hours—it’s about cycles and quality. Sleep Reset changed everything." —Lauren, 29 Ready to Go Beyond a Bedtime Guess? You’ve got your result from the sleep time calculator—now make it count. Sleep Reset helps you turn bedtime into real, restful sleep by addressing the underlying reasons you might be struggling. Read more about CBTI - the gold standard for getting a good night's sleep! Start your free sleep quiz to get a personalized sleep plan rooted in CBT-I! Start your sleep quiz Sleep Calculator Questions People Also Ask What Is a Sleep Calculator? A sleep calculator is a tool that determines the best time to fall asleep or wake up based on 90-minute sleep cycles. It helps you wake up between cycles instead of during deep sleep, reducing grogginess. Is 10 PM to 4 AM enough sleep? No. That’s only 6 hours (4 cycles). Most adults need 7–9 hours. What time should I sleep if I wake at 5 AM? Try: 9:30 PM (7.5 hours) 8:00 PM (9 hours) How do sleep cycles work? Each cycle lasts ~90 minutes. Waking between cycles reduces grogginess. Is 6 hours of sleep enough? Only for a small percentage of people. Most need at least 7 hours. How many sleep cycles do you need per night? Most adults need 4–6 sleep cycles per night. Each cycle lasts about 90 minutes, so this equals 6 to 9 hours of sleep. How long does it take to fall asleep? On average, it takes 10–20 minutes to fall asleep. When using a sleep calculator, you should factor this in. What happens if you wake up in the middle of a sleep cycle? Waking during deep sleep can make you feel groggy and disoriented, a phenomenon known as sleep inertia. Is it better to wake up after 6 hours or 7 hours? 6 hours aligns with 4 sleep cycles, while 7 hours interrupts a cycle. In many cases, 6 hours may feel better than 7—but 7.5 hours is ideal. What time should I go to bed if I wake up at 4 AM? Try: 8:30 PM (7.5 hours) 7:00 PM (9 hours) What time should I sleep if I wake up at 6 AM? Try: 10:30 PM (7.5 hours) 9:00 PM (9 hours) What is the best bedtime for waking up early? The best bedtime depends on completing full 90-minute cycles. For most people, this means going to bed between 9 PM and 11 PM. Can I train my body to wake up without an alarm? Yes. By maintaining a consistent sleep schedule aligned with your circadian rhythm, your body can naturally wake up without an alarm. Why do I still feel tired after 8 hours of sleep? Poor sleep quality, frequent awakenings, or misaligned sleep cycles can leave you feeling tired even after enough hours. What is sleep inertia? Sleep inertia is the groggy feeling you experience when waking up from deep sleep. It can last from a few minutes to over an hour. Does napping affect sleep cycles? Yes. Long or late naps can disrupt your nighttime sleep cycles and make it harder to fall asleep. How do I fix a broken sleep schedule? Gradually shift your bedtime by 15–30 minutes each night and maintain consistent wake-up times, even on weekends. What is REM sleep and why does it matter? REM sleep is the stage where dreaming occurs and is essential for memory, learning, and emotional regulation. What is deep sleep? Deep sleep is the most restorative stage of sleep, crucial for physical recovery and immune function. What is a circadian rhythm? Your circadian rhythm is your body’s internal clock that regulates sleep and wake cycles over a 24-hour period. Can you catch up on sleep? You can recover some sleep debt, but inconsistent sleep patterns can still negatively affect your health.

title: Which DIY Repair Saved You the Most Money?
summary: Be it an automobile or any other product, a repair job usually takes three elements: the correct diagnosis, the appropriate replacement part(s), and the requisite labor to perform the repair. Repairs are often a team effort; just look at how many folks are required to run a service center. But there are plenty of enterprising […]
body_text: Be it an automobile or any other product, a repair job usually takes three elements: the correct diagnosis, the appropriate replacement part(s), and the requisite labor to perform the repair. Repairs are often a team effort; just look at how many folks are required to run a service center. But there are plenty of enterprising individuals out there who believe they can do it by themselves. These do-it-yourself (DIY) repairs are a big part of automobile ownership, and they are easier than ever these days. Why? Not only are many repair tools accessible and affordable, but the information is readily available online. We have dedicated repositories like ALLDATA , traditional automotive forums , social media groups (Facebook, Reddit, etc.), content creators on YouTube, and—should you prefer physical media—even automotive literature resellers on eBay. I generally like forums and YouTube videos for detailed explainers on a given matter, as they have saved me countless hours. My job writing about cars on the Internet has intensified the issue, as DIY-ers inspire many pieces in my portfolio. I’ve likely done enough work to save myself six figures, so I really appreciate folks who spend the time to share their knowledge with others. We all have to start somewhere, and I wish I had a video like this one from YouTube creator/personal friend Brad Hansen when I began my DIY journey many decades ago. Hansen does a great job setting you up for success, not necessarily by teaching you how to do the repair, but how to get your mind ready for a DIY task. While I enjoyed this particular video, it was more of a refresher course for yours truly. My most recent DIY effort included YouTube to ensure I correctly installed a rear window for my Ranger, after demoting that glass from a prominent display location inside my house . Aside from the color-matched rain gutter popping itself loose on the driver’s side, the conversion from a (leaky) sliding rear window to a single-piece affair went quite nicely. Sajeev Mehta Sajeev Mehta I was lucky enough to have the garage, the tools, and the time/motivation to DIY this project. Doing so probably saved me a hundred or so bucks in labor, and that felt great. It also feels great to share these thoughts with others, so here’s the question I propose to you fine folks: What DIY repair saved you the most money and how did you learn to do it? For me, it’s likely DIY heater-core replacements (shivers) . The post Which DIY Repair Saved You the Most Money? appeared first on Hagerty Media .

Castellino to Chief Information Officer July 29, 2026 MILWAUKEE--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Marcus Corporation (NYSE: MCS) today announced that Rajiv W. Castellino, chief technology officer of Marcus Hotels & Resorts, has been promoted to chief information officer of Marcus Corporation. Castellino will assume the role on August 2, 2026, succeeding Kim M. Lueck, who will retire as chief information officer on August 1, 2026, after nearly 30 years with the company. “Rajiv has consistently aligned technology strategies to drive revenue, improve efficiency, and strengthen the long-term success of Marcus Hotels & Resorts,” said Gregory S. Marcus, chief executive officer of Marcus Corporation. “I am confident he will bring the same focus and discipline as he assumes leadership of our enterprise-wide technology strategy and infrastructure. Castellino holds a master’s degree in management information systems from the University of Dallas in Irving, Texas, a master’s degree in marketing from Symbiosis Institute of Business Management in India, and a bachelor’s degree from Ferguson College of the University of Pune in India. title: Kalshi launches biotech prediction markets pilot program
summary: Kalshi and AppliedXL are launching a pilot suite of prediction markets on clinical trial outcomes and FDA regulatory decisions, making drug-development probabilities publicly available for the first time.
body_text: Kalshi, the next-generation financial exchange, today announced a partnership with public intelligence company AppliedXL to launch a pilot suite of prediction markets on clinical trial outcomes and FDA regulatory decisions. The markets will create publicly available, accurate probabilities aiming to help solve drug development's information silo problem. The odds that a drug will succeed are among the most valuable numbers in the economy, and among the least visible. The average cost to bring a single drug to market is an estimated $2.3 billion, according to McKinsey, and a company's fortunes can turn on a single trial result. Banks, expert networks, and pharmaceutical companies all produce estimates, but they stay behind closed doors. Even the official public record is incomplete: as of the FDA's April 2026 figures, roughly 30% of trials required to report their results had posted none. These markets close that gap. A publicly listed contract on a trial or regulatory outcome produces a continuously updated, public probability that reflects the weight of the evidence rather than the preferred messaging of the trial sponsor. Because the price now moves on the public record rather than on privileged access, people who were never in the room — investors allocating capital, smaller developers weighing where to compete, clinicians and patients tracking a program — can all read the same number. ❝ "Drug development is one of the most important and most information-constrained industries on earth. The data that determines which drugs advance and which don't is largely locked away from the people who need it most. Surfacing information is what Kalshi is for, and we are committed to doing it right: compliance-first, carefully scoped, and built for the long term." — Tarek Mansour, CEO, Kalshi The markets also give investors something they have never had: a way to act on a view about a single drug. Public equities force a position on the whole business at once — on management, cash, pipeline, and macro together. An investor can be right about the science or the regulatory outcome and still watch the stock move the other way. These contracts isolate the single question. Owning the stock is still owning the whole company; a contract prices the science or the regulatory outcome on its own terms. How the markets resolve AppliedXL, a public intelligence company tracking pharmaceutical data, provides the resolution infrastructure underpinning the markets. Each contract specifies a named public document as its resolution source: the registered primary endpoint on ClinicalTrials.gov — meaning the main result the trial was designed to measure — the FDA approval letter, or the advisory committee vote record. AppliedXL defines the criteria for reading that document before the contract opens for trading, not after results arrive. Outcomes are determined by independent public artifacts, not by sponsor communications or analyst interpretation, making resolution transparent, auditable, and resistant to dispute. ❝ "Clinical trial results are rarely handed to you cleanly. They come out in pieces, scattered across registries, regulatory filings, and company statements, and the press releases often put a favorable spin on what the data actually shows. Resolving a market means reconciling all of that back to the primary source, which is what we built AppliedXL to do." — Francesco Marconi, AppliedXL Example contracts available at launch include: Will AR1001's POLARIS-AD Phase 3 trial meet its primary endpoint in early Alzheimer's disease? Will the FDA approve Gilead/Arcellx's anito-cel for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma? Alongside today's launch, Kalshi and AppliedXL are publishing Biopharma's Public Probability : The State and Future of Prediction Markets in Drug Development , a joint whitepaper drawing on interviews with clinicians, academics, biopharma R&D and strategy professionals, bioethicists, and investors. It examines the opportunities and challenges these markets present, and the standards required for them to function reliably. Scope and safeguards These initial markets are a pilot program, deliberately constrained to protect both the integrity of the markets and the integrity of the trials they price. Working with biopharma R&D and strategy professionals, biotech investors, physicians, and bioethicists, Kalshi and AppliedXL built two design choices into the pilot: Late-stage trials. Earlier-phase contracts involve exploratory endpoints and greater insider trading risk. Late-stage trials register their primary endpoints publicly, often after agreeing them with the FDA in advance, making resolution unambiguous. Listing only after enrollment closes. A visible market price could influence physician referral and recruitment. Kalshi and AppliedXL list a contract only after a trial finishes enrolling. Employment verification. Kalshi will require employment verification for all traders in these markets as an additional integrity measure. On top of these pilot-specific choices, Kalshi's existing rules apply in full. The prohibition on trading by anyone who holds material nonpublic information applies here exactly as it does in every other Kalshi market. Kalshi and AppliedXL will study how these markets perform and how traders engage with them, using what they learn to refine the market design and the guardrails ahead of any potential broader release.

title: Enhance & Upscale Sora Video to 4K | Flick
summary: Sora shut down, but your exports can still get better. Upscale Sora video to 4K, de-flicker, and color-grade your clips in one Flick canvas.
body_text: Sora shut down on April 26, 2026. The API followed on September 24, but OpenAI still offers users the oppurtunity to export their remaining Sora data. Whatever your videos look like today is what they'll look like forever — unless you enhance them. This guide covers exporting your archive, upscaling it to 4K, fixing Sora's known artifacts, and continuing unfinished projects with current models. Why Sora footage is still worth enhancing Sora produced some of the most-watched AI video ever made. That is why the exports are worth saving: once the service is gone, these clips become both source footage and historical reference material for whatever you make next. First: export your Sora archive before it's deleted Go to sora.chatgpt.com/sunset . Select Export . Wait for the email — exports are prepared asynchronously. Download the archive and back it up somewhere you control. What you're actually working with Spec Sora export Resolution Pro: up to 1080p · Plus: 720p Clip length Pro: up to 20s · Plus: about 10s Watermark Visible watermark + C2PA provenance metadata on every export Container MP4 Aspect ratios 16:9 and 9:16 Three defects show up in most Sora footage: Temporal flicker: lighting and texture shimmer between frames, especially on skin, skies, water, fabric, and flat walls. Soft fine detail: hair, fabric weave, signage, text, eyelashes, and background edges look smeared or airbrushed above 1x zoom. Identity morphing: faces, hands, wardrobe details, and props drift over longer clips, so the subject at the end of the shot is not quite the subject from the first frame. Upscale Sora videos to 4K The safest workflow is non-destructive: keep the original Sora export untouched, create a new enhanced master, and use that master for editing, color, and publishing. Import your exported MP4 into a Flick canvas. Open the clip enhancement or upscale tool. Set the target resolution to 4K. Preview at 100% and 200% crop, not just full-frame. Export a new master while preserving the original file. What upscaling does well: Recovers apparent sharpness. Reduces compression artifacts. Makes 720p or 1080p exports hold up better on large screens. Creates a cleaner master for editing, grading, and republishing. What upscaling does not do: It cannot reconstruct detail Sora never generated. It cannot fully fix identity drift across a shot. It cannot remove every temporal artifact. It should not be used to remove Sora's watermark or provenance metadata. Enhance your footage in Flick Upscale, de-flicker, and grade your clips on one canvas. Best settings for Sora upscaling Use the source clip to decide how aggressive your enhancement should be. Source problem Recommended approach What to watch for Soft but stable footage 2x–4x upscale with moderate sharpening Avoid crunchy edges and plastic skin Heavy flicker De-flicker before final upscale Too much smoothing can erase intentional texture Low detail backgrounds Light denoise + upscale Do not over-sharpen smeared details Face or hand drift Local repair or re-generation Upscale alone will not solve identity changes Compression blocking Denoise, then upscale Preserve grain if the clip has a filmic look A good rule: if the clip looks fake after enhancement, reduce the strength. The goal is a cleaner Sora master, not a hyper-sharpened demo frame. "RIP Sora, you gave us the greatest AI video of all time." Credit: @sporadica on X . The best Sora video enhancers in 2026, compared Tool Price Max upscale Batch Works on Flick Less than 1¢ per second of input video Up to 4K Project-based workflow Any clip inside a full editing canvas Topaz Video AI $299 perpetual + $99/year updates Up to 16x Yes Any local file Krea $35/month Pro · $70/month Max 8K–22K plans Platform-dependent Any clip; video upscale requires Pro+ Topaz is the desktop standard for pure upscaling: strong, local, and built for file-based workflows. Krea is fast and accessible if you already work inside its generation platform. Higgsfield bundles enhancement into a credit system, which can be harder to price for a full archive. Flick's difference is workflow. The upscale happens inside the same project where you can keep editing, grading, repairing, and generating new shots. That matters for Sora archives because the job is rarely just "make this one file larger." The job is usually "turn old Sora footage into a usable film asset." Fix Sora footage, not just sharpen it 1. De-flicker and stabilize motion Temporal flicker is one of the fastest ways to make AI footage feel unfinished. Run de-flicker before your final export, especially on clips with: Faces and skin. Skies, water, and smoke. Flat walls or studio backdrops. Fabric with fine texture. Slow camera moves. If motion feels choppy, interpolate to 30fps or 60fps after de-flicker. Do not overdo it: aggressive interpolation can introduce warped edges or a soap-opera look. To achieve this easily, you can use the edit video feature on Flick’s canvas with Kling or Gemini video edit. This will reproduce your exact video, without the flicker and instability. Use the following prompt: “Reproduce the exact video, keeping audio, objects, characters, etc 100% unchanged and exact. Remove the choppy interpolation and stabilize the video, keeping all other aspects the same.” 2. Unify the color grade Clips generated months apart often do not match. Sora's look shifted across versions, prompts, and styles, so an archive can feel like fragments from different projects. A single color pass can fix more perceived quality than an upscaler: Match exposure across shots. Normalize contrast. Pull skin tones into the same range. Add a consistent film grain or texture layer. Use the same black point and highlight rolloff across the sequence. To achieve this easily for an image, you can use the color grade feature inside of Flick’s timeline editor. Upload your image to Flick’s canvas, and then tune the lighting, color, split tone, and effects to your liking. To normalize the contrast and exposure across shots, pay special attention to the exposure and contrast sliders. You can add a vignette with the vignette slider. For even more control, and to expand this process to videos as well, I recommend using a third party video editor like After Effects, Final Cut Pro X, or Davinci Resolve. 3. Repair local artifacts If only part of a frame is broken — a hand, a sign, a face edge, a background object — do not re-roll the entire shot. You may never get the same composition again. Instead: Choose the best frame or short section. Mask the broken region. Regenerate or repair only that area. Blend it back into the original shot. Upscale after the repair pass. This is especially useful for hands, teeth, text, logos, reflections, and background faces. To achieve this easily on Flick’s canvas, you can upload your image and use the inpaint tool to highlight a specific section. Then specify to the model, I prefer Nano Banana 2 for precise high quality edits, or Pruna, which is significantly cheaper but slightly lower quality, exactly what you want to change. Be sure to remind the model to keep the existing aspects of your image, like the character, style, and lighting, 100% exact and unchanged. Continuing a Sora project when Sora is gone The real problem is not sharpness. The real problem is that you may have fourteen usable shots and the model that made them no longer exists. The method is to turn your Sora archive into reference material: Pull character frames from your strongest Sora shots. Build a reference pack with multiple angles, wardrobe details, closeups, and full-body frames. Identify which shots are locked and which shots need new coverage. Generate matching coverage with a current model. Animate your characters with state of the art video models like Seedance 2.0 and Kling o3 Pro. Cut everything together in one timeline. Your Sora footage stops being a dead archive and becomes casting material for the rest of the film. Build a reference pack from Sora footage A strong reference pack should include: Identity frames: clear face angles, neutral expressions, and the most consistent version of the character. Wardrobe details: sleeves, collars, shoes, jewelry, props, and silhouettes. Lighting references: the key look from the scene you want to continue. Motion references: frames that show posture, walk cycle, gestures, or how the subject carries themselves. Negative examples: frames where the character drifted, so you know what not to match. Current models such as Seedance, Kling, Veo, and other multi-model workflows can use those references to create new coverage that feels connected to the original project. The result will not be identical to Sora, but with careful reference selection and grading, it can be close enough to finish the film. Common mistakes to avoid Publishing the raw export without checking it at full size. Many defects only show up at 100% or 200%. Over-sharpening. This makes AI artifacts more obvious. Fixing color last. Grade early enough to know which clips actually match. Deleting originals. Always preserve the untouched Sora export. Treating every clip as final footage. Some clips are more valuable as character or style references than as publishable shots. Trying to remove provenance. Leave watermarking and metadata alone. Frequently Asked Questions Can I still download my Sora videos? Yes. Go to sora.chatgpt.com/sunset, select Export, and download the archive when the email arrives. OpenAI deletes remaining data after the export window closes, so do it now rather than later. Can Sora videos be upscaled to 4K? Yes. Exported 720p or 1080p clips can be upscaled to 4K with modern video enhancement tools, including inside a Flick canvas. Upscaling sharpens what exists; it cannot reconstruct detail the model never generated. Will upscaling remove the Sora watermark? No — and do not try. The watermark and C2PA metadata identify the clip as AI-generated, which is important for provenance and trust. What replaced Sora? For filmmaking, current options include Seedance, Kling, Veo, and multi-model editing canvases such as Flick. The best choice depends on whether you need character consistency, motion quality, reference control, or fast iteration. Why did OpenAI shut down Sora? OpenAI discontinued the Sora app on April 26, 2026 and is retiring the API on September 24, 2026. Its help center focuses on the export process rather than a detailed shutdown rationale. What should I do first with a large archive? Export, back up, and catalog everything before enhancing anything. Once you know which clips are final footage, which need repair, and which are best used as references, the enhancement workflow becomes much faster.

title: How to Build an App Store Listing (2026): 14 Key Elements
summary: The world’s most powerful AI app studio. Build real native iOS apps one step at a time.
body_text: TL;DR Your app store listing is the single page that determines whether someone downloads your app or keeps scrolling. With over 1.8 million apps on the App Store and most getting fewer than 100 downloads in their first month, every element matters. This guide covers all 14 components of a high-converting listing, from app name to localization, with exact specs, conversion data, and the mistakes that get apps rejected. Average iOS listing conversion sits around 25%, but optimizing each element can push that number significantly higher. An App Store listing is made up of 14 core metadata and visual elements that determine how your app ranks in search and converts visitors into downloads. The most important ranking elements on iOS are the App Name, Subtitle, and Keywords field, while the biggest conversion drivers are your App Icon, Screenshots, Ratings, and App Preview Video. Optimizing every element together—not individually—produces the highest App Store conversion rates and better App Store Optimization (ASO) results. App Store Listing Components at a Glance Component Helps Rankings Helps Conversion Required App Name ✅ High ✅ High Yes Subtitle ✅ High ✅ Medium Yes Keywords ✅ High ❌ iOS Only Description Google Play Only ✅ Medium Yes App Icon ❌ ✅ High Yes Screenshots ❌ ✅ Very High Yes Preview Video ❌ ✅ High Optional Ratings & Reviews ✅ Moderate ✅ High Automatic Privacy Details ❌ Trust & Compliance Yes Localization ✅ ✅ Optional Why Your App Store Listing Is the Only Page That Matters Roughly 70% of app installs originate from app store search. That means for most apps, especially indie ones without ad budgets, the store listing is the entire marketing funnel. It’s the billboard, the landing page, and the checkout counter rolled into one. Here’s the uncomfortable math: AppTweak’s H1 2024 data shows iOS store pages convert about 25% of visitors, while Google Play averages 27.3%. That means three out of four people who see your listing leave without downloading. Most users decide within 3 seconds whether to install or move on. The good news? Most of your competition is doing this badly. Practitioners on indie developer forums consistently report that a focused, research-driven approach to their listing moved them from invisible to top 10 for valuable keywords within weeks. The bar is low. Clearing it requires understanding what each element does and how to make it work. If you’re building an app from scratch and want one place to handle everything from planning through App Store submission, see how x1 works end to end. This guide walks through every element of a complete app store listing, the specs Apple and Google require, the conversion impact of each piece, and the common mistakes that lead to rejection. At-a-Glance: Every App Store Listing Element Element Character/Size Limit Indexed for iOS Search? Conversion Impact Update Frequency App Name 30 characters Yes (strongest factor) High Rarely (brand risk) Subtitle 30 characters Yes High Each version App Icon 1024×1024 PNG No Up to +22.8% lift Test quarterly Screenshots 1–10 images, specific sizes No +21.7% uplift 2–4× per year App Preview Video Up to 30 sec, up to 3 videos No +20% to +47% lift As features change Description 4,000 characters No (iOS) / Yes (Google Play) Low (1% read fully) Each version Keywords Field 100 characters Yes Critical Each version Promotional Text 170 characters No Low (timely messaging) Anytime Category Primary + Secondary No Moderate (Top Charts) Rarely In-App Purchases 20 items, 35-char names Appear in search results Moderate As pricing changes Ratings & Reviews N/A Influences ranking High Ongoing Privacy & Age Rating Required fields No Rejection risk if missing Each version Localization Per-market versions Per-language fields Up to +8.6% lift Each version What’s New No hard limit No Low (retention-focused) Each version How an App Store Listing Works Most developers think of an App Store listing as a page that describes an app. In reality, it serves three different purposes simultaneously. Discovery Apple indexes selected metadata fields to determine which apps appear for a search query. Conversion Visual assets such as the icon, screenshots, preview video, ratings, and pricing persuade users to install. Compliance Metadata must comply with Apple's App Review Guidelines. Incorrect privacy information, misleading screenshots, trademark violations, or inaccurate descriptions can delay approval or result in rejection. Thinking of your listing as three systems working together—search visibility, conversion, and compliance—helps prioritize improvements. 1. App Name Best for: Discoverability. Your app name is the single most important ranking factor in the App Store. Specs: Maximum 30 characters Must be unique and not infringe on trademarks Displayed in search results, charts, and your product page Best practices: Include your most important keyword naturally. If your app is a meditation timer, “Calm Timer” beats “SereniFlow.” Keep it simple and easy to spell. Users who can’t remember your name can’t search for it. Don’t stuff it with keywords. Apple explicitly warns against packing metadata with generic terms or competitor names, and doing so is a common reason for rejection. Tradeoffs: You only get 30 characters, so there’s genuine tension between brand identity and keyword inclusion. Changing your app name after launch resets brand recognition. Get it right early. What goes wrong: Apple’s guidelines state that app names should not include pricing information, irrelevant phrases, or terms designed to game the system. One of the fastest paths to rejection is cramming your title with keywords that don’t accurately describe what the app does. 2. Subtitle Best for: Expanding on your name with a keyword-rich value proposition. Specs: Maximum 30 characters Appears below your app name throughout the App Store Indexed for search on iOS Best practices: Complement, don’t repeat, the app name. If your name contains “Budget,” your subtitle shouldn’t also say “Budget.” Use those 30 characters for different searchable terms. Explain the value. “Track Spending in Seconds” tells users what they get. “World’s Best Finance App” tells them nothing (and violates Apple’s guidelines against generic superlatives). Treat this as your second-most-valuable keyword slot after the title. Tradeoffs: Only 30 characters forces hard prioritization. You can’t fit everything. Updated only with new app versions, so you can’t A/B test quickly. On iOS, Apple’s algorithm focuses on a limited set of text fields. Your app name, subtitle, and the hidden keyword field are the only places where keywords directly influence search rankings. The long description does not get indexed. This makes every character in your subtitle count. 3. App Icon Best for: First impressions. The icon is the very first visual element users see in search results. Specs: 1024×1024 pixels, PNG format, no transparency Apple automatically resizes for different contexts (home screen, search results, settings) Best practices: Keep it simple with one focal element. The best icons read clearly at 60×60 pixels on a phone screen. Make it distinctive enough to stand out in a grid of competitors. Convey your app’s core function visually without relying on text. Conversion impact: SplitMetrics found icon changes can improve conversion by up to 30%. AppTweak’s 2025 benchmarks show a +22.8% uplift on the App Store from icon optimization alone. That’s a massive return for what seems like a small design decision. Tradeoffs: Icon A/B testing on iOS requires Apple’s Product Page Optimization feature, which has limited traffic allocation. Radical icon changes can confuse existing users who search for the familiar image. Testing tip: Change the symbol or focal subject, not just colors. Color shifts rarely produce statistically significant results, but switching from an abstract shape to a recognizable object often does. 4. Screenshots Best for: Conversion. Screenshots are the highest-impact visual element on your listing. Specs: 1 to 10 screenshots per device size Required sizes for iPhone: 6.9-inch displays (1290×2796 or 1320×2868 pixels) and 6.5-inch displays (1284×2778 or 1242×2688 pixels) Displayed in search results and on your product page Best practices: Lead with benefits, not features. “See your savings grow weekly” beats “Dashboard with chart view.” The biggest mistake is screenshots that show what the app does instead of what the user’s life looks like after using it. Front-load your strongest two images. Only 17% of visitors scroll past the first screenshot. The first two do most of the heavy lifting. Use text overlays sparingly and make them readable at thumbnail size. Update screenshots 2–4 times per year. Top-performing apps treat screenshots as living marketing assets, not set-and-forget uploads. Conversion impact: Screenshots show a +21.7% uplift potential on the App Store and +24.3% on Google Play. Sensor Tower found that simply reordering screenshots (same images, different sequence) drove 6.4% more installs in a 30-day test. The order matters as much as the content. The DIY vs. tool debate: Practitioners on Reddit report that many indie iOS developers still prefer making screenshots manually in Figma using iPhone device templates because the results feel more polished. AI screenshot generators save significant time, but the templates can feel generic. The right choice depends on how much design control matters to you versus how much time you can spend. If you’re using an end-to-end AI app studio that generates native iOS apps, the screenshots reflect real native UI rather than mockups, which matters for both conversion and Apple’s requirement that screenshots show actual app interface. What Makes a High-Converting Screenshot? The highest-converting screenshots usually follow a consistent structure. State the user's biggest benefit. Show the feature that delivers it. Keep overlay text under 8 words. Use one message per screen. Maintain consistent branding across all images. Avoid clutter, tiny text, and feature lists that are difficult to read on mobile devices. 5. App Preview Video Best for: Demonstrating complex features or workflows that screenshots can’t convey. Specs: Up to 30 seconds per video Up to 3 app preview videos Must show actual app functionality (no external footage or misleading content) Best practices: Lead with the most compelling moment in the first 5 seconds. Don’t waste time on logos or intros. Design for muted viewing. Most users won’t tap for sound. Use text overlays and visual storytelling. Show the app solving a real problem, not a feature tour. Conversion impact: StoreMaven data suggests preview videos produce roughly a +20% lift in conversion. On iOS, where videos autoplay in search results, the impact jumps to +47%. On Google Play, only about 6% of visitors actually tap to play a video, so the ROI is much lower there. Tradeoffs: Production quality matters. A bad video hurts more than no video at all. Videos must show actual app UI, which means you need a working build before you can create them. File size and encoding requirements are strict. Apple rejects videos that don’t meet spec. 6. Description Best for: Providing context for users who want more detail before downloading. Specs: Up to 4,000 characters Updated only with new app versions (unlike promotional text) Best practices: Front-load everything important into the first sentence. That’s what users see without tapping “more,” and only about 1% of people read the full description. Write for humans, not algorithms. On iOS, the long description is not indexed for keyword search. Your keywords field handles that. Structure with short paragraphs and bullet points for scannability. Focus on outcomes. A common mistake is treating app listings like feature sheets. Users care about how the app improves their lives. iOS vs. Google Play difference: This is critical. On Google Play, the long description IS indexed for keywords, so natural keyword placement matters there. On iOS, stuffing keywords into your description accomplishes nothing for search ranking. Write your iOS description purely for conversion. If you’re a first-time builder trying to turn an app idea into a real app , the description is where you tell the human story of why this app exists. Lead with the problem, show the solution, and keep it short. Recommended Description Structure A strong App Store description usually follows this framework: One-sentence value proposition Three to five key benefits Core features Social proof or credibility Call to action Most users only read the first few lines, so place the most persuasive information first. 7. Keywords Field (iOS Only) Best for: Search ranking on the App Store. This hidden field is surgically important. Specs: Exactly 100 characters total Comma-separated, no spaces between terms Not visible to users Best practices: Use all 100 characters. Every unused character is wasted ranking potential. Separate keywords with commas only (no spaces). The system interprets them automatically. Don’t duplicate words that already appear in your app name or subtitle. Apple already indexes those. Avoid trademarked terms and competitor names. Improper keyword use is a common reason for App Store rejections. Update keywords with each app version based on performance data. Practical keyword research: The simplest and most underrated keyword research tool is the App Store search bar itself. Start typing a word related to your app and observe the autocomplete suggestions. These are real terms that real users are actively searching for. Tradeoffs: 100 characters is extremely limited. You’ll agonize over every word. No built-in analytics from Apple on keyword performance. Third-party tools (AppTweak, Appfigures, ASOdesk) fill this gap but add cost. Testing keywords requires submitting new versions, which means slower iteration cycles. 8. Promotional Text Best for: Timely messaging that doesn’t require a new app submission. Specs: Up to 170 characters Appears above the description on your product page Can be updated anytime without submitting a new version Best practices: Use this for seasonal promotions, new feature announcements, or event tie-ins. Don’t waste it on keywords. Apple explicitly states promotional text doesn’t affect search ranking. Refresh it regularly to signal active development to browsing users. Tradeoffs: No search ranking benefit means this is purely a conversion play. 170 characters limits what you can say. Treat it like a tweet, not a paragraph. Many developers forget this exists and leave it blank, which is a missed opportunity. 9. Category Selection Best for: Appearing in the right Top Charts and browse tabs. Specs: One required primary category One optional secondary category Determines which tab and charts your app appears in Best practices: Choose the category that most accurately describes your app’s primary function. Apple may reject your app if the category is misleading. Consider competition density. A less competitive secondary category can give you more visibility in Top Charts even if your primary category is crowded. Tradeoffs: Wrong category selection can result in rejection during App Review. Changing categories later may reset your chart position. Some apps genuinely fit multiple categories, forcing a compromise. 10. In-App Purchases & Subscriptions on Listing Best for: Transparency and discoverability of your monetization model. Specs: Up to 20 items displayed across in-app purchases and subscriptions You choose the display order Names: 35 characters max Descriptions: 55 characters max Best practices: Lead with your most popular or highest-value offering. Write descriptions that emphasize what the user gets, not what it costs. Ensure exact price matching between your listing metadata and in-app pricing. A mismatch, even one dollar, can trigger rejection and delay your launch by a week or more. In-app purchase items can appear in App Store search results and featured sections, making them an underappreciated discovery channel. Practitioners report that well-named IAP items sometimes rank for keywords the main listing doesn’t target. For guidance on navigating the full app launch and review process , including pricing and subscription compliance, that linked guide covers common pitfalls. 11. Ratings & Reviews Best for: Social proof and ranking signals. High ratings both improve search position and reassure visitors. Specs: Star rating (1–5) based on user reviews You can prompt for ratings using SKStoreReviewController up to 3 times in a 365-day period Developer responses are visible on the product page Best practices: Use the rating prompt strategically. Trigger it after a positive moment (completing a task, reaching a milestone) rather than on first launch. Respond to every negative review within 48 hours. This shows potential users you’re actively maintaining the app, and sometimes the reviewer updates their rating. Never incentivize reviews. Apple prohibits it and will reject or remove your app. Tradeoffs: You only get 3 prompts per year per user. Timing matters enormously. Early negative reviews can tank conversion before you have enough volume to recover the average. Resetting ratings on a major version update is sometimes worth it, sometimes not. It depends on whether your new version genuinely fixes the complaints. 12. Privacy Information & Age Rating Best for: Compliance. Getting these wrong is the fastest path to binary rejection. Specs: Privacy policy URL required for all apps Age rating determined through Apple’s questionnaire (Apple assigns the final rating) Privacy nutrition labels must accurately reflect data collection practices Privacy manifests required for certain APIs and third-party SDKs Best practices: Complete the privacy questionnaire honestly. Misrepresenting data collection practices leads to removal, not just rejection. Keep your privacy policy URL active and updated. A dead link triggers rejection. Account for all third-party SDKs in your privacy manifest. Missing manifests have been one of the most common binary rejection causes from 2024 through 2026. Context: In 2026, Apple reviewed around 7.77 million app submissions and rejected nearly 25%, approximately 1.93 million, for failing to meet quality, safety, or design requirements. Privacy and metadata issues account for a significant share of those rejections. 13. Localization Best for: Reaching non-English markets without additional development work. Specs: Localize app name, subtitle, keywords, description, screenshots, and promotional text per market Custom Product Pages allow tailored listings for different audiences and campaigns Best practices: Even basic translation outperforms showing English to non-English users. You don’t need perfect localization to see gains. Localize your keywords field separately for each language. Direct translations often miss the actual search terms people use in that market. Localize screenshots. Users in Japan expect different visual communication norms than users in Brazil. The underutilized opportunity: Custom Product Pages remain surprisingly rare. Only 31% of apps and 26% of games use them, yet those who do see conversion lifts up to +8.6%. These pages let you create different listing variations for different ad campaigns or audience segments. Tradeoffs: Localization multiplies your maintenance burden. Every listing update needs to happen across all supported languages. Poor translations can actually hurt worse than English-only listings. Custom Product Pages require enough traffic volume to produce statistically meaningful test results. 14. What’s New (Version Notes) Best for: Retention and re-engagement with existing users. Specs: No hard character limit (though Apple recommends keeping it concise) Displayed on your product page under “What’s New” Updated with each new version submission Best practices: List new features in order of importance. Lead with what users actually asked for. For minor bug-fix releases, simple language like “Bug fixes and performance improvements” is fine. Include a brief call-to-action when appropriate: “Try the new dark mode in Settings.” Tradeoffs: Version notes have minimal impact on new user conversion. They matter more for existing users deciding whether to update. Overpromising in release notes and underdelivering erodes trust and invites negative reviews. Which App Store Listing Elements Affect Rankings? Not every field influences App Store search rankings. Many developers spend hours optimizing descriptions that Apple doesn't even index. Ranking Factors Element Indexed by Apple Search App Name Yes Subtitle Yes Keywords Field Yes In-App Purchase Names Sometimes Ratings & Reviews Indirectly Description No Promotional Text No Screenshots No Videos No Knowing which fields actually affect rankings helps prioritize optimization efforts. Recommended Order for Optimizing an App Store Listing If you're launching a new app, optimize your listing in this order. App Name Subtitle Keywords Icon Screenshots Ratings Preview Video Description Localization Promotional Text This order prioritizes elements with the largest impact on visibility and conversion. Apple App Store vs Google Play Listing Differences Although both stores share many listing elements, several important differences affect optimization. Feature Apple App Store Google Play Description indexed No Yes Hidden keywords Yes No Subtitle Yes Short Description Promotional Text Yes No Custom Product Pages Yes Custom Store Listings Product Page Optimization Yes Store Listing Experiments Understanding these differences helps developers avoid applying Google Play ASO tactics to the App Store. Common Listing Mistakes That Get You Rejected Apple’s review team catches more listing problems than most developers expect. Here are the metadata-related rejection reasons that come up repeatedly: Keyword stuffing. Cramming unrelated terms, competitor names, or trending phrases into your app name, subtitle, or keywords field. Apple’s guidelines are explicit: keep the 30-character app name relevant and use the 100-character keywords field for legitimate variations only. Screenshots that don’t match actual UI. Your screenshots must show the real app interface. Mockups, aspirational designs, or screenshots from a different version will be flagged. Price mismatches. If your listing metadata says $4.99 but your in-app price shows $5.99, Apple will reject you. A one-dollar mismatch can cost you a week. This is one of those surprise rejection reasons that trips up even experienced developers. Missing demo credentials. If your app requires login, you must provide working test credentials for the review team. Forgetting this is embarrassingly common and entirely preventable. Promising features not yet built. Your description and screenshots must reflect the current, shipping version. Describing upcoming features as if they already exist violates Apple’s guidelines. Misleading categories. Selecting a category your app doesn’t belong in, hoping for less competition, risks outright rejection. For non-technical founders navigating this process for the first time, the rejection rate can feel intimidating. But most rejections are preventable with careful attention to metadata accuracy. Metrics to Track After Publishing Publishing your listing is only the beginning. Monitor these key performance indicators regularly. Metric Why It Matters Impressions Search visibility Product Page Views Listing traffic Conversion Rate Download efficiency Downloads Overall growth Keyword Rankings Discoverability Retention Listing quality Average Rating Social proof Crash Rate User experience Review these metrics after every significant listing update to determine whether changes improved performance. How to Build and Launch Your Listing Without Tool Sprawl Creating a complete app store listing involves writing copy, designing an icon, creating screenshots, selecting keywords, setting up privacy labels, and submitting for review. Most developers cobble together five or six different tools for this, and each handoff introduces friction and errors. The pattern that works for indie developers and small teams: pick tools that handle multiple listing elements in one workflow. Keyword research tools like AppTweak or Appfigures cover the analytics side. Screenshot generators like AppLaunchpad or Rotato handle visuals. But the bigger problem is that most AI app builders stop at code generation. They hand you a project file and wish you luck with everything that comes after: screenshots, metadata, submission. x1 takes a different approach. Its Launch studio creates App Store screenshots, writes the listing copy, and handles submission in the same environment where you built the app. Because x1 generates native Swift and Xcode apps, the screenshots reflect real native UI, not web wrapper approximations. This matters both for conversion (users can tell) and for Apple’s requirement that screenshots show actual app interface. Explore x1’s pricing plans to see which tier fits your launch timeline. If you’re comparing different AI app builder approaches , the key question is whether the tool covers the last mile: listing assets, ASO metadata, and the submission workflow itself. Most don’t. App Store Listing Optimization Checklist Use this checklist before submitting every version. App name contains primary keyword naturally Subtitle communicates value Keywords field uses all available characters Screenshots show actual app UI First screenshot explains the primary benefit Preview video demonstrates real functionality Description starts with the value proposition Privacy labels are accurate Category is correct Prices match in-app purchases Test credentials included Localization reviewed Promotional text updated Version notes completed Frequently Asked Questions How many screenshots do I need for my App Store listing? Apple requires between 1 and 10 screenshots for iPhone apps. While the minimum is 1, you should use at least 5 or 6 to tell a complete story. The first two screenshots matter most since only 17% of visitors scroll beyond the first one. Does the app description affect search rankings on iOS? No. On iOS, the long description is not indexed for keyword search. Only your app name, subtitle, and the hidden keywords field influence search rankings. On Google Play, the description IS indexed, so keyword placement matters there. Write your iOS description purely for conversion, not search optimization. How often should I update my app store listing? Top-performing apps update their screenshots 2–4 times per year and refresh keywords with each version release. Promotional text can be updated anytime without a new submission, making it ideal for seasonal or timely messaging. What causes App Store listing rejections? The most common listing-related rejection causes include keyword stuffing, screenshots that don’t match actual app UI, price mismatches between metadata and in-app pricing, misleading category selection, and missing privacy information. Apple rejected nearly 25% of the roughly 7.77 million submissions it reviewed in 2026. What’s the difference between promotional text and the description? Promotional text (170 characters) can be updated anytime without submitting a new app version and appears above the description. It’s not indexed for search. The description (4,000 characters) can only be changed with a new version submission and, on iOS, is also not indexed for search. Use promotional text for timely updates and the description for your evergreen value proposition. How do Custom Product Pages work? Custom Product Pages let you create different versions of your App Store listing for different audiences or ad campaigns. Only 31% of apps currently use them, but those that do see conversion lifts up to +8.6%. They’re one of the most underutilized tools in App Store optimization. What size should my app icon be? Submit a 1024×1024 pixel PNG file with no transparency. Apple automatically resizes this master icon for all display contexts, from the home screen to search results to settings. Icon optimization alone can drive conversion improvements of up to 22.8%. Can I use competitor names in my keywords field? No. Apple prohibits using trademarked terms or competitor app names in your metadata, including the hidden keywords field. Violating this rule is a common cause of rejection and can result in your app being removed from the store entirely.

title: Hear Michelle Branch's The Spirit Room 25th Anniversary Performance on SiriusXM
summary: The singer-songwriter performs her hits live, plus shares stories about collaborating with The New Radicals and more on PopRocks.
body_text: Michelle Branch celebrated the 25th anniversary of her breakthrough album, “The Spirit Room,” with an exclusive performance in front of a live audience on PopRocks (Ch. 6) . Michelle Branch LIVE Celebrating 25 years of “The Spirit Room” Listen on the App Listen on the App Recorded at the SiriusXM Los Angeles studios, “Michelle Branch LIVE” featured unforgettable performances of “All You Wanted,” “Breathe,” “Everywhere,” and “The Game of Love.” Between songs, Michelle reflected on the enduring impact of “The Spirit Room” and shared the story behind collaborating with The New Radicals on a new version of “The Game of Love.” She also explained why revisiting the hit alongside one of her longtime musical inspirations made the project especially meaningful. Stream “Michelle Branch LIVE” in full exclusively on the SiriusXM app. View this post on Instagram

title: Achieve Life Sciences Announced Granting of New Hire Inducement Awards
summary: SEATTLE and VANCOUVER, British Columbia, July 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Achieve Life Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACHV), a late-stage…...
body_text: Achieve Life Sciences Announced Granting of New Hire Inducement Awards July 31, 2026 8:30am EDT Download as PDF SEATTLE and VANCOUVER, British Columbia, July 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Achieve Life Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACHV), a late-stage specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the global development and commercialization of cytisinicline as a treatment for nicotine dependence, today announced that Achieve’s board of directors approved stock option grants to purchase an aggregate of 1,190,000 shares of its common stock and restricted stock unit (“RSU”) awards covering an aggregate of 125,000 shares of its common stock for six new employees under Achieve’s 2024 Equity Inducement Plan. The stock options have an exercise price equal to the closing price of Achieve’s common stock on the grant date. Each stock option has a four-year term and will vest as to 25% of the shares underlying the stock option on the first anniversary following commencement of employment. The remaining 75% of the shares underlying the stock option will vest in 36 equal monthly installments thereafter, subject to the employee’s continued service through each applicable vesting date. Each RSU award represents the right to receive one share of Achieve’s common stock upon vesting, subject to the recipient’s continued service. The RSUs will vest over four years with 25% of the underlying shares vesting on each anniversary following commencement of employment, subject to the employee’s continued service through each applicable vesting date. The stock options are subject to the terms and conditions of the 2024 Equity Inducement Plan, as well as the terms and conditions of the stock option agreement covering the grant and were made as an inducement material to the individual entering into employment with Achieve in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). About Cytisinicline There are approximately 25 million adults in the United States who smoke combustible cigarettes.¹ Cytisinicline is a plant-based alkaloid with a high binding affinity to the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. It is believed to aid in treating nicotine addiction for smoking and e-cigarette cessation by interacting with nicotine receptors in the brain, reducing the severity of nicotine craving symptoms, and reducing the reward and satisfaction associated with nicotine products. About Achieve Life Sciences, Inc. Achieve Life Sciences, Inc. is a late-stage specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the global development and commercialization of cytisinicline as a treatment of nicotine dependence. Achieve’s New Drug Application (NDA) for cytisinicline for smoking cessation in adults is supported by two successfully completed Phase 3 studies and an open-label long-term safety study. Achieve has also completed a Phase 2 study of cytisinicline in nicotine e-cigarette cessation, conducted an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA, and has received Breakthrough Therapy designation for the vaping cessation indication. Forward Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the “safe harbor” provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including, but not limited to, statements Achieve makes regarding the timing, nature and outcome of cytisinicline clinical development and regulatory review and approval, data results, the timing, nature and success of Achieve’s commercialization activities, the potential market size for cytisinicline, the potential benefits, efficacy, safety and tolerability of cytisinicline, the development and effectiveness of new treatments, the performance of Achieve’s third-party manufacturing partners, the successful launch and commercialization of cytisinicline, and statements concerning Achieve Life Sciences’ future plans and prospects. All statements other than statements of historical fact are statements that could be deemed forward-looking statements. Achieve may not actually achieve its plans or product development goals in a timely manner, if at all, or otherwise carry out its intentions or meet its expectations or projections disclosed in these forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management’s current expectations and beliefs and are subject to a number of risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially from those described in the forward-looking statements, including those described in Achieve’s Annual Reports on Form 10-K and Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q. Achieve undertakes no obligation to update the forward-looking statements contained herein or to reflect events or circumstances occurring after the date hereof, other than as may be required by applicable law. Achieve Contact Nicole Jones VP, Strategic Communications and Stakeholder Relations ir@achievelifesciences.com 425-686-1510 Reference ¹Agaku I.
